title: CrowdStrike says China-based suspect used AI tools in South Korean bank hacks
source_used: Reuters text as carried by The Japan Times (Reuters byline and SEOUL dateline)
key_facts: CrowdStrike published a report on its website on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 about the South Korean financial-sector attacks.
The suspect may be a 26-year-old based in China's Guangdong province, according to the report; CrowdStrike says the available information could not definitively identify the attacker.
The campaign targeted South Korean financial institutions from late September to early October 2026.

The attacker used ARTEX, a recently released Chinese-developed open-source penetration testing tool, alongside large language models; CrowdStrike assesses with moderate confidence that the actor is a Chinese speaker and likely financially motivated.

Banks including Shinhan Bank and KB Kookmin Bank reported data breaches; Seoul authorities are investigating and South Korean police have launched a probe, which had not yet responded to a request for comment.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that signs had emerged that AI was used in some of the hacking incidents.
quote_evidence: The company said the personal details likely belonged to the actor responsible for the activity, but cautioned that currently available information could not definitively identify the attacker.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that signs had emerged that AI was used in some of the hacking incidents and called for heightened cybersecurity measures.
why_it_matters_hint: AI tools were used in attacks that led to reported data breaches at South Korean banks; the attacker is not identified.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (CrowdStrike report); attacks late Sep to early Oct 2026
